8.25.21.en: First: since Christ is Wisdom, we must see that He Himself was the beginning of the ways of God's works. I think there is no doubt about this, since He says, "I am the way: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me"... Therefore He was created for the beginning of the ways and works of God, because He is the Way and leads men to the Father..

8.25.22.en: Second: He was created for the works of God from the beginning of the ages when He submitted Himself to the form of visible creation, bearing the form of a created being.

8.25.23.en: St. Hilary of Poitiers * Let no one be confused by the words "before the world," and "before he had made the earth," and "before the mountains were settled".. For there is here an allusion to the economy according to the flesh. Although the grace that came upon us from the Savior has now appeared, as the Apostle says, and came when He dwelt among us, yet this grace was prepared even before we existed. Indeed, it was prepared before the foundation of the world, and the reason for it is His wonderful tenderness.

8.25.24.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic "While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the highest part of the dust of the world" [26].

8.25.25.en: "When he prepared the heavens, I was there: when he set a compass upon the face of the depth" [27].

8.25.26.en: * The Wisdom of God, by whom all things were made, was there; Wisdom Himself works in holy souls and makes them friends of God, and His prophets, and speaks to us of His works in quietness.

8.25.27.en: St. Augustine * Let us learn also that the Father was with Him, and He was with the Father when all things were created.

8.25.28.en: Wisdom says, "When he prepared the heavens, I was with him, when he made the fountains of waters."

8.25.29.en: And in the Old Testament, when the Father says, "Let us make," He showed that the Son must be worshipped with Him as the maker of all things, since it is said that these things were created by the Son.

8.25.30.en: St. Ambrose * Who was with Him when He created all existence, if not His Wisdom, who says, "When he made the heaven and the earth, I was with him"? By referring to heaven and earth He refers to all the creatures that are in heaven and on earth. For being present with Him as His Wisdom and His Word, looking to the Father as He created, ordered, and gave order to the universe, and being the power of the Father, He gives power to all things, and as Savior He says, "What things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise" (Jn 5:29; 1:16). And His holy disciples knew that all things were created by Him and for Him.

8.26.0.en: 30 Then I was by him, as a craftsman: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him; 31 Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men.

8.26.1.en: "I was by him, as a craftsman (administrator)" [30].

8.26.2.en: The divine hypostasis of Wisdom affirms His role in creation. As the Evangelist John says: "All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made" (Jn 1:3), and the Apostle Paul says: "By whom also he made the worlds" (Heb 1:2); "For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him" (Col 1:16).

8.26.3.en: "And I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him" [30].

8.26.4.en: This affirms the relationship of mutual love between the two hypostases, the Father and Wisdom. If the Father planned that the Son should accomplish salvation, it is because the Father's delight is in His Son, and the Son's delight is in His Father. So the redemption accomplished by the Son, "the Wisdom of God," is ascribed to the Father, as the Lord Christ says: "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son" (Jn 3:16). Thus Wisdom's accomplishment of redemption is also a giving up by the Father, who loves Wisdom and is one with Him.

8.26.5.en: * I am the one in whom He (the Father) delights. Moreover, I was daily His delight before Him.

8.26.6.en: He rejoiced in the world that He had created, and in the sons of men..

8.26.7.en: With God is Wisdom, begotten before the worlds, not only present with Him, but ordering the worlds together with Him..

8.26.8.en: Observe His work in managing and ordering things. The Father by His command is the cause, and the Son manages and orders by carrying out what has been commanded. The distinction between the two hypostases lies in the work belonging to each.

8.26.9.en: When it was said, "Let us make" (Gen 1:26), creation was made known by the word of command, and when it was written, "I was by him as a craftsman," God declares that He did not make it alone (apart from the Son). For He was His joy before Him.. He rejoiced in the world He made and in the sons of men.

8.26.10.en: Wisdom tells us the reason for His joy. He rejoices at the joy of the Father, who rejoices at the completion of the creation of the world and of the sons of men. For it is written: "And God saw that it was good" (Gen 1:10, 12, 31).. His Wisdom is a partner with Him in the work and rejoices with Him as He completes the work.

8.26.11.en: St. Hilary of Poitiers * Is it not counted blasphemy to say that there was a time when the Wisdom of God did not exist?! He said: "I was by him as a craftsman, I was his delight daily."

8.26.12.en: Or to say that the power of God did not exist, or His Word, or anything else by which the Son is known, or to which the Father points, is this not an error?!

8.26.13.en: Whoever says that the brightness of the glory of the Father did not exist at some time destroys the original light, which is the brightness....

8.26.14.en: Pope Alexander of Alexandria * Therefore the eternal brightness shines before Him and exists with Him, in the same existence that has no beginning, and is begotten always, and always shines before Him. He is the Wisdom who says, "I was with him, his delight; I was his delight always before his face..."

8.26.15.en: St. Dionysius the Great * His Wisdom is the one in whom is His delight always, as in His Spirit. He is one with Him as the soul of God, and stretches out like a hand to form the universe.

8.27.0.en: The Clementine Homilies "Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men" [31].

8.27.1.en: If Wisdom declares that He is the object of the Father's delight, being one with Him and the Creator, then in turn He draws His delight in us, His creation, who disobeyed Him and rebelled against Him.

8.28.0.en: 32 Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children: for blessed are they that keep my ways. 33 Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not. 34 Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.

8.28.1.en: Finally, after Wisdom has declared the plan of His incarnation, which arises from His love and the Father's love for the sons of men, and His desire that we be the object of His good pleasure and delight, He calls us to listen to Him and to receive Him, so that we may enjoy the blessed life.

8.28.2.en: The Lord Christ says: "Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death" (Jn 8:51).

8.28.3.en: "Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children: for blessed are they that keep my ways" [32].

8.29.0.en: "Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not" [33].

8.30.0.en: "Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors" [34].

8.30.1.en: * He who has the light is watchful, "and the darkness comprehended it not" (Jn 1:5), and he does not sleep, since there is no darkness.

8.30.2.en: He who is enlightened is wakeful toward God; thus he lives.

8.31.0.en: "For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour (will) of the LORD" [35].

8.31.1.en: The Wisdom of God asks us not only to listen to Him but to find Him and possess Him, as the Lord Christ says: "He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life" (Jn 3:36).

8.31.2.en: Wisdom offers Himself to the human soul, and it must seek Him and find Him. Here seeking means the will, for Wisdom does not force His way into the human soul without its will; rather, when it seeks Him in complete freedom, it finds Him present. This holy will is also a gift from God, as the Apostle says: "For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure" (Phil 2:13).

8.31.3.en: * For man it is not good not to will, but by the grace of God he receives help to will, for it is not in vain that it is written: "For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure" (Phil 2:13); and that "the will is prepared of God."

8.32.s.en: 7. The misery of those who reject the call

8.32.0.en: "But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul:

8.32.1.en: all they that hate me love death" [36].

8.32.2.en: The Lord Christ Himself says: "He that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him" (Jn 3:36). He also says: "For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will" (Jn 5:20). And the beloved John says: "He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life" (1 Jn 5:12).

8.32.3.en: Let me possess You and enjoy life!

8.32.4.en: * Your voice resounds in my inner ears.

8.32.5.en: Let me ascend with You to the summits of the high mountains, to enjoy the splendor of Your glory on Mount Tabor, to delight in Your pure blood on Mount Golgotha, and to experience the company of the angels on the Mount of Temptation.

8.32.6.en: * When I find myself wandering, I see You standing on the way, waiting for me at the crossroads, carrying me on Your royal road, and bringing me into the bosom of Your Father.

8.32.7.en: * When my soul groans in distress, at the gates I find You a just Judge!

8.32.8.en: You hear all the troubles of my soul, and when the world wrongs me, I find You my defender!

8.32.9.en: * Let me hear Your voice and enjoy Your wisdom.

8.32.10.en: Your wisdom is the food that comes down from heaven.

8.32.11.en: It satisfies my soul and waters it.

8.32.12.en: It gives me a transcendent life, before which all the treasures of the world become very small.

8.32.13.en: * Let me possess You, O Wisdom of God, my beloved Jesus!

8.32.14.en: Then I will love goodness and hate all evils.

8.32.15.en: You give me good counsel and strength with honor.

8.32.16.en: You fill the storehouses of my soul with blessings that never perish!

8.32.17.en: * For my sake You became incarnate and became man, that I may meet You as a Savior and a personal friend.

8.32.18.en: You are the good pleasure of the Father; You have made me the object of Your pleasure and delight every day!

8.32.19.en: * Let me possess You and possess the light, so that there is no more darkness or night in me, and my eye does not slumber, but I remain watchful.

8.32.20.en: I enjoy the blessed life, and I receive partaking in the divine nature!

8.32.21.en: * Yes, whoever finds You finds eternal life!

8.32.22.en: And whoever sins against You acquires death!

8.32.23.en: You are my life, my joy, and my glory!

9.0.0.en: 1 Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars: 2 She hath killed her beasts; she hath mingled her wine; she hath also furnished her table. 3 She hath sent forth her maidens: she crieth upon the highest places of the city, 4 Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him, 5 Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled. 6 Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding. 7 He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked man getteth himself a blot. 8 Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee: rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee. 9 Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning. 10 The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding. 11 For by me thy days shall be multiplied, and the years of thy life shall be increased. 12 If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself: but if thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear it.

9.0.1.en: The wise Solomon reviews the concern of the Wisdom of God for the heavenly table that He has prepared for His beloved, the sons of men, who are the object of His good pleasure and delight, showing its cost and its effectiveness in their lives. He speaks of the following:

9.1.s.en: A. The house of the banquet

9.1.0.en: Every emperor, king, or head of state takes care to set aside a main part of his palace for holding banquets, especially for emperors, kings, or presidents, and also for statesmen, officials, and others. The banquet hall reveals the person's concern for those he invites, and it also makes known the character of the one who gives the banquet. For this reason the building bears a national character that reveals the civilization of the country, its resources, and so on. But the Wisdom of God did not build a house to invite others to it; rather, He took on our human nature, becoming truly man. The house became not foreign to Him, but His own house. His divinity was united with His humanity without separation and without mixture. So the invitation He extends to us is that we abide in Him and become members of His body. It is an invitation to eternal union with Him!

9.1.1.en: He opened the doors of His house, that is, His body, not only when He opened His mouth before the crowds in the Sermon on the Mount, nor when He spoke with us on the level of the congregation as well as on the personal level, with each one of us, but when He allowed His side to be opened on the cross to pour out blood and water for us. His side is open at all times so that we may enter into His house and touch the bowels of His fiery love, and so enjoy continual existence with Him and in Him. As the Giver of the banquet Himself says: "Abide in me, and I in you" (Jn 4:15). And the Apostle Paul says: "Your life is hid with Christ" (Col 3:3).

9.1.3.en: The house that the Wisdom of God built is the humanity of the Lord Christ. God's eternal plan prepared the Incarnation so that salvation might be accomplished.

9.1.4.en: * Let us look at Christ from both sides: the divine Word who became one in Mary with the one He took from Mary. For in her womb the Word formed for Himself a house, just as in the beginning He formed Adam from the earth.. Or rather, as the wise Solomon said plainly, knowing that the Word is called Wisdom: "Wisdom hath builded her house," which the Apostle interpreted, saying: "whose house are we," and in another place he calls us a temple. If it was fitting for God to dwell in a temple made after a certain pattern, built of stones, He commanded the ancient people through Solomon to build it, whereas at the appearing of the truth the pattern ceased (for the truth itself appeared).

9.1.5.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * But we say that in the first part of the book, where it says, "Wisdom hath builded her house," he points in an obscure way through these words to the preparation of the body of the Lord, for the transcendent Wisdom did not dwell in another's dwelling, but built for Herself a dwelling from the body of the Virgin... Thus we can see in this passage Solomon moved by the spirit of prophecy, delivering to us in it the fullness of the mystery of the Incarnation.

9.1.6.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa * Here we surely recognize that the Wisdom of God, that is, the Word, who shares eternity with the Father, built for Himself a house, that is, a human body in the womb of the Virgin, and subjected the Church to Him as members to the Head. He slew the martyrs as sacrifices and prepared a table with bread and wine, having established the priesthood after the order of Melchizedek. He called the simple and those who lack sense, as the Apostle says: "God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty" (1 Cor 1:27).

9.1.7.en: St. Augustine * The testimony of St. Gregory of Nyssa in his book Against Eunomius:

9.1.8.en: "The Word was before all the ages, but the flesh was made in the fullness of time, and no one can say the opposite, that the flesh was before the ages, or that the Word was made in the fullness of time.

9.1.9.en: Theodoret * Christ, meaning the wisdom and power of God, built a house for Himself, that is, His nature in the flesh which He took from the Virgin, as John says: "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us." This is as the wise prophet bears witness: the Wisdom who was before the world, the source of life, the Infinite, "the Wisdom of God hath builded her house" by means of a mother who knew not a man, that is, He took the temple of the body.

9.1.10.en: St. Hippolytus Holy Scripture declares that the Holy Trinity shared in accomplishing the divine Incarnation, or in establishing the house of the banquet, for it devised the plan of salvation, and the divine Wisdom built a house for Himself, and the divine Incarnation was accomplished by the work of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the holy Virgin Mary, who thereby received a unique honor. And the wonder is that the Wisdom of God also builds by His Holy Spirit a house for Himself in us, a dwelling for the Holy Trinity, as He says: "My Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him" (Jn 14:23).

9.1.11.en: * Just as we read that the Father wrought the mystery of the Lord's incarnation, and the Spirit also, so we read that Christ Himself made His body.

9.1.12.en: Of the Father it is written: "The LORD possessed me" (Prov 8:22), and in another place: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

9.1.13.en: And the Spirit wrought the whole mystery, as we read: "Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

9.1.14.en: St. Ambrose From our inner man He builds a wonderful house of banquet, which the soul calls "his garden," as it speaks to the Wisdom of God, saying: "Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits" (Song 4:16). And the divine Wisdom answers her invitation, saying:

9.1.15.en: "I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse:

9.1.16.en: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey;

9.1.17.en: I have drunk my wine with my milk:

9.1.18.en: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved" (Song 5:1).

9.1.19.en: This is the house that the Wisdom of God builds in us and counts as His house and His garden, and to it He invites His heavenly friends to eat and drink and rejoice in the fruit of His wonderful Holy Spirit in us.

9.1.20.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa comments on this invitation which the human soul extends to the One who made a garden of it and turned its depths into a rich banquet, saying:

9.1.21.en: [Who is this whom the bride invites to her banquet, which bears its own fruits?

9.1.22.en: For whom has she prepared a banquet from her own (inner) resources?

9.1.23.en: Who is this whom the bride invites to the banquet she has prepared? None other than the One of whom and through whom and to whom are all things (Rom 11:36). He gives every one their meat in due season (Ps 145:15), He opens His hand and fills all living with His blessings. He came down as bread from heaven (Jn 6:41), and gave life to the world, and made the waters burst forth from His fountain of life. This is the One for whom the bride prepares her table.

9.1.24.en: The table is a garden planted with living trees.

9.1.25.en: We are indeed the trees, and the food offered to Him is the salvation of our souls.]

9.1.26.en: It is the work of the Wisdom of God to tear down the old tent, which is the works of the old man that sin has raised up in us, in order to build a new inner house, renewed every day. "Though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day" (2 Cor 4:16).

9.1.27.en: This house which the Lord Christ built is His holy Church, in which He presents Himself as a living stone, rejected of men, but chosen of the Father and precious (1 Pet 2:4); He bears us as living stones resting upon Him, built beside one another and united together to become like one tower. As St. Peter the Apostle says: "Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ" (1 Pet 2:5).

9.2.s.en: B. The strength and stability of the house

9.2.0.en: "She hath hewn out her seven pillars" [1].

9.2.1.en: If the Wisdom of God has built a house for Himself, taking our humanity and making it one with Himself, then He hewed out seven pillars on which to set the building. What are these pillars but His fiery Spirit, one with Him? This Spirit, who cannot be separated from Him, He has given us by building our inner man as a house for Himself, so that we are supported by Him, and He leads us with power to the inexhaustible pastures of Christ and brings us into His eternal Kingdom, granting us strength, victory, and transcendent consolations.

9.2.2.en: * It is impossible for anyone to receive the grace of God unless he has the Holy Spirit, in whom are all the gifts of God.

9.2.3.en: St. Didymus the Blind * (The Holy Spirit) is called "the Comforter" because He comforts and gladdens those who are in tribulations.

9.2.4.en: St. Macarius the Great * When the soul is filled with the fruit of the Spirit, it is fully comforted from sadness, distress, and weariness, and it puts on spaciousness, peace, and joy in God, and the door of love for all people is opened in its heart.

9.2.5.en: Mar Isaac the Syrian * "She hath hewn out her seven pillars," that is, the sweet fragrance of the all-holy Spirit, as Isaiah says: "And the seven spirits of God shall rest upon him." Some see the pillars as the seven orders upon which creation stands by His holy and inspired teaching, namely the prophets, the apostles, the martyrs, the priests, the solitaries, the saints, and the righteous.

9.2.6.en: * He means the new Jerusalem and the holy body. And by the seven pillars he means the sevenfold unity of the Holy Spirit resting upon them.

9.2.7.en: St. Hippolytus * Concerning the dignity of the number seven we have many testimonies, but we content ourselves with a few of the many. For example: seven precious spirits are named, for I think Isaiah likes to call the activities of the Spirit spirits; and the teachings of the Lord are purified seven times, as David says (Ps 12:6); and the righteous is delivered from six troubles, and in the seventh no evil shall touch him. The sinner is forgiven not seven times, but seventy times seven. We can also see this by the opposite (for the punishment of the wicked is praised): vengeance was taken for Cain sevenfold, and when the punishment for the killing of his brother was carried out, it was exacted for Lamech seventy times sevenfold, because he was a murderer according to the Law and was condemned. And wicked neighbors receive sevenfold into their bosom, and the house of Wisdom rests on seven pillars, and the stone of Zerubbabel is adorned with seven eyes, and God is praised seven times a day, and also the barren woman bears seven, the perfect number, in contrast to her whose children are imperfect.

9.3.1.en: What does the Lord Christ offer in His house but His body given up, a sacrifice of love, which the Father smells as a sweet savor, and which He offers to His believers as a transcendent heavenly table?

9.3.2.en: * This table is the support of our souls, the bond of our mind, the foundation of our hope, our salvation, our light, and our life.

9.3.3.en: * When you see the table prepared before you, say to yourself:

9.3.4.en: Because of His body I am no longer dust and ashes, nor a prisoner, but free!

9.3.5.en: Because of this (body) I hope for heaven, and I receive the heavenly goods, immortal life, the portion of the angels, and converse with Christ!

9.3.6.en: This body was nailed with nails and scourged, and death no longer has power over it!

9.3.7.en: It is the body that was stained with blood and pierced, and from it came forth the two fountains that save the world: the fountain of blood and the fountain of water.

9.3.8.en: St. John Chrysostom As we partake of this unique sacrifice, we long to share with our Christ His sacrificial love, so that we offer sacrifices of love without ceasing. As the teacher Tertullian says: [This sacrifice goes forth from the whole heart, is nourished by faith, observes the truth, enters in innocence and purity, in chastity, and is adorned with love. We must guard it with the greatness of good works, offering psalms and hymns on the altar of God so that we may receive all things from Him.]

9.3.9.en: With the Apostle Paul we offer the sacrifice of daily suffering and sing, saying: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress.. As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter" (Rom 8:25, 26). By the cross of our Lord the ego is slain, and we say: "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I," boasting that the slain Christ has become alive in us.. and we say: "but Christ liveth in me" (Gal 2:20).

9.3.10.en: We offer the sacrifice of humility before God (Ps 51:16, 17), the sacrifices of righteousness (Ps 4:5), the sacrifice of the body held in check by the cross of the Lord (Rom 12:1), the sacrifice of praise (Heb 13:15).

9.3.11.en: * I myself would like to be numbered among her children, that I may be slain by her. I would like to be slain in order to be a son.

9.3.12.en: But is she a slayer of her children, or a tormentor of them? For I hear God say also in another place: "I will burn them as gold in the fire, and I will try them as silver is refined." Surely it is by the pains of fire and punishments and by the trial of martyrdom for the faith.

9.3.13.en: The Apostle also knows a kind of slaying which he describes to us: "He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?"

9.3.14.en: Behold how the divine Wisdom slays even what is her own!

9.3.15.en: The only-begotten firstborn Son is slain, who not only lives but gives life to others. I say: He is the Lord Christ who gives Himself for our transgressions.

9.3.16.en: Tertullian * The phrase "she hath killed her beasts" refers to the prophets and martyrs who were killed in every city and nation by unbelievers for the sake of the truth, and who cry out, saying: "For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter."

9.4.1.en: The ancient Jews, Greeks, and Romans seldom drank wine without mixing it with water, and many ancient writers have dealt with this matter. Some see the mixing of wine with water at a ratio of 3 to 1, others 5 to 1, and Pliny noted that some wines require the addition of 20 measures of water, but the great majority hold that 3 measures of water are added to 2 measures of wine.

9.4.2.en: Some, however, do not mix wine with water to weaken its strength but mix it with spices or honey or myrrh, or madragora or opium and the like, to increase the sharpness of the wine, so that it not only intoxicates but also stupefies. Perhaps the mixing also refers to blending it with precious kinds of wine so as to bring a man joy and gladness of heart.

9.4.3.en: The Wisdom of God offers us His pure blood as a spiritual, heavenly drink. As it is said in the Liturgy of Bishop Serapion: [We offer to You this bread.. and this cup.. Make all who partake of it receive the medicine of life, healing for every weakness, support for all progress and virtue, and not judgment upon us.]

9.4.4.en: * Moreover, the Holy Spirit shows through the wise Solomon the order of the sacrifice of the Lord, pointing to the sacrifice offered of bread and wine. And also concerning the altar and the apostles he says: "Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars, she hath killed her sacrifices, she hath mingled her wine in the cup, she hath also furnished her table. She hath sent forth her maidens, she crieth upon the highest places of the city, Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither. And as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him, Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled." He proclaims the mingled wine, and also tells us beforehand with a prophetic voice of the cup of the Lord mingled with water and wine, which is shown to have been fulfilled in the passion of our Lord, of which prophecy was made beforehand.

9.4.5.en: St. Cyprian * The phrase "she hath mingled her wine" in an earthen vessel means that the Savior unites His divinity with the body like pure wine in the Virgin, born of her as God and man at the same time without mixture between them.

9.4.6.en: St. Hippolytus * Since they abandon milk, they drink wine that gladdens the hearts of those who are more perfect, who no longer practice childish things. Now they have become able to drink the good things from the cup of Wisdom with their mouths.

9.4.7.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa The Wisdom of God offers us the cup of wine, which is His blood shed for us for the forgiveness of our sins, and with it the cup of wisdom, that by it we may understand the mysteries of Holy Scripture and receive a spiritual knowledge that is effective in our lives.

9.4.8.en: * Those who receive symbols from Holy Scripture according to the understanding of the disciples enjoy the hope that the saints truly eat; indeed it will be the bread of life that refreshes the soul with the food of truth and wisdom, enlightens the mind, and makes it drink from the cup of divine wisdom according to the declaration of Holy Scripture.

9.4.9.en: Origen If wine points to spiritual joy, then as we partake of the holy blood and drink from the cup of wisdom, a true joy is born in us that supports the soul and waters it, so that it does not faint on the path of suffering.

9.5.s.en: E. The order of the banquet

9.5.1.en: By saying that she "furnished" or "prepared" her table, Holy Scripture affirms that this banquet, though free and with its doors open to every human being, is a banquet prepared by the Lord Himself. For long generations He prepared mankind through the fathers and the prophets to enter it. The banquet has its order and arrangement, because the One who prepared it is a God of order and not of confusion (1 Cor 14:32).

9.6.s.en: F. The invitation to the banquet

9.6.0.en: "She hath sent forth her maidens: she crieth upon the highest places of the city,

9.6.1.en: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither:

9.6.2.en: as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,

9.7.0.en: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled" [3-5].

9.7.1.en: Wisdom sent her maidens to the tops of the hills and the heights and the mountains to cry out, for it is a general and public invitation, because God wills that all be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth. It was the custom anciently in some Asian cities that a person would send to those invited a company of maidservants, preceded by some eunuchs, and they would deliver the invitation to the feast.

9.7.2.en: St. Clement of Alexandria sees these messengers as the prophets who went before the Lord, whom He sent to invite them to the banquet; these are not thieves or robbers, but philosophy was not sent by the Lord, and so it came to steal. He means here the philosophies opposed to the truth and resisting the knowledge of God.

9.7.3.en: * The phrase "she hath furnished her table" refers to the knowledge of the Holy Trinity that was promised, and also to His precious pure body and blood, which are offered every day as a sacrifice on the divine spiritual table, a perpetual remembrance of the first divine spiritual supper.

9.7.4.en: St. Hippolytus The cry of the invitation is directed to the one who feels that he is simple, that he may turn aside and enjoy divine wisdom, and the one who feels that he lacks understanding comes forward to enjoy the table of true knowledge.

9.7.5.en: * In this house of the banquet, those who come from the east and the west find a place for themselves in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven.

9.8.s.en: G. The effectiveness of the banquet

9.8.0.en: "Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding" [6].

9.8.1.en: When the believer responds to the public, free call of Wisdom, it is fitting for him to show his response to this call by forsaking foolishness and walking in the way of understanding, through the riches of the grace of God working in him. He asks us to forsake ignorance and the foolish, for whoever keeps company with them necessarily becomes foolish like them.

9.8.2.en: * That (the table of demons) is a mingling with demons, but this (the table of the Lord) is fellowship with God.

9.8.3.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem * The mystical table is the body of the Lord, which supports us against our passions and against Satan.

9.8.4.en: Truly Satan trembles at those who partake of these mysteries with reverence.

9.9.s.en: H. The seriousness of the banquet

9.9.0.en: "He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked man getteth himself a blot.

9.10.0.en: Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee: rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee" [7-8].

9.10.1.en: The philosophers thought that they were without sin and formed a special class immune from error, but the word of God reveals the weakness of human nature and the need of all, even the teachers and leaders, for continual learning.

9.11.0.en: * Is this perhaps the reason that there is no one, even among those who dare to call themselves wise, because they (the philosophers) think that the wise man is without sin? But our Holy Scripture does not say this; it says: "Rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee" [8]. Without doubt, whoever thinks that a man must be rebuked judges that he is a sinner.

9.11.1.en: In any case, for my part I do not dare to count myself wise even in this sense. It is enough for me to count myself what they cannot deny, that the struggle for wisdom is ascribed to the philosophers, that is, to the lovers of wisdom. For those who practice the love of wisdom do not cease to struggle for wisdom, and these are counted wiser than they.

9.11.2.en: St. Augustine The invitation is directed to all, but only the man who is serious about the salvation of his soul perceives it. For this reason the scorner, finding in the invitation a rebuke of his carelessness, instead of responding to the call of Wisdom insults the one who offers it to him, and the wicked man who is determined to remain in his wickedness, instead of repenting, ascribes faults and evils to the one who cares for his salvation.

9.11.3.en: It is not strange that "unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath" (Mt 25:29). He who has wisdom increases in wisdom, because he seeks to grow in it, and he loves the one who teaches and rebukes him that he may obtain knowledge. But he who has a spirit of mockery, scorn, and evil grows worse in evil, because he bears hatred toward the one who rebukes or guides him.

9.12.0.en: "Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning" [9].

9.12.1.en: He did not say, "Give teaching to a wise man," but "Give to a wise man," without specifying what you offer him. For the wise man benefits from everything that is given to him; he is like the bee that gathers honey from every flower.

9.12.2.en: St. John Chrysostom sees among his people wise men who need him to begin some of his meditations on Holy Scripture with them to open the way, while they complete what he began and add to it, growing in wisdom.

9.12.3.en: * It would be fitting for us to present all the other points, but this would make the discourse very long, and extend over a very long time. For this reason we stop presenting other points, and leave this matter to you, for it is within your power to have it in your hands. It is within your power to gather these points together at home and examine the differences, and in the same way you will perceive new points. It was said: "Give the beginning of the place to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser" [9 LXX]. The beginning is from us, but the end is with you.

9.13.s.en: I. The way of the banquet

9.13.0.en: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding" [10].

9.13.1.en: We cannot enter the way of Wisdom unless we seek the fear of the Lord, for it is the beginning of wisdom, and it is also its goal. We begin with the divine fear that accompanies us all along the way until it brings us into the divine embrace. We enjoy a fear mingled with love, not the fear of slaves that casts out love, but the fear of sons who enjoy the spirit of love.

9.13.2.en: The teacher Tertullian, in his attack on philosophy and the philosophers, says that the philosophers fail to know God, and are doubtful, and fall into confusion because they have lost the fear of the Lord.

9.14.s.en: J. The extension of the banquet

9.14.0.en: "For by me thy days shall be multiplied, and the years of thy life shall be increased" [11].

9.14.1.en: Wisdom grants a multitude of days and an increase in the years of life. Whether the days of the believer's life on earth are short or long, in the eyes of God they are fruitful and extended, and death cannot destroy them.

9.15.s.en: K. The one who benefits from the banquet

9.15.0.en: "If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself: but if thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear it" [12].

9.15.1.en: What a man sows he reaps: if he sows wisdom, he enjoys it, and if he sows mockery and scorn, he harms no one but himself.

9.15.2.en: * No one shares in the spiritual table except the one who is called by (God), and who listens to the Wisdom that says: "Come, eat."

9.15.3.en: St. Dionysius the Great He who experiences Wisdom comes to her hungry, seeking her not to receive temporal blessings, but to possess her, and Jesus ben Sirach expressed this in a wonderful poem on the search for Wisdom with which he closed the book, in which he said:

9.15.4.en: [In my youth, before I went astray, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer.

9.15.5.en: Before the temple I asked for her, and I will seek her out even to the end.

9.15.6.en: My heart delighted in her blossom, as in a grape when it ripens.

9.15.7.en: My foot walked in the straight way.

9.15.8.en: From my youth I followed her track. I inclined my ear a little and received her.

9.15.9.en: And I found for myself much instruction.

9.15.10.en: I made progress by her, and to him who gave me wisdom I will give glory, for I purposed to practice her, and I was zealous for the good, and I shall not be put to shame.

9.15.11.en: I strove with my soul for her, and I observed the Law with great exactness.

9.15.12.en: I stretched out my hands to the heights, and I bewailed my ignorances.

9.15.13.en: I directed my soul to her in purity, and I found her.

9.15.14.en: With her I gained understanding from the beginning, therefore I shall not be forsaken.

9.15.15.en: My bowels were stirred in seeking her, therefore I have gained a good possession.]

9.16.0.en: 13 A foolish woman is clamorous: she is simple, and knoweth nothing. 14 For she sitteth at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city, 15 To call passengers who go right on their ways: 16 Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: and as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him, 17 Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant. 18 But he knoweth not that the shades are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.

9.16.1.en: "A foolish woman is clamorous: she is simple, and knoweth nothing" [13].

9.16.2.en: If the table of Wisdom was prepared and arranged by God Himself, offering divine resources which the believer enjoys in order to become wise and a possessor of knowledge, and to grow in both, then the table of folly is offered by the foolish woman. Perhaps by the foolish woman he means evil itself. He describes her as follows:

9.16.3.en: a. Foolish: without wisdom or true knowledge.

9.16.4.en: b. Clamorous: she causes a clamor that is meaningless and carries no love, but only noise and anxiety.

9.16.5.en: c. Simple: she acts with stupidity.

9.16.6.en: d. Haughty: she sits at the door of her house on a seat in the high places of the city, teaching the spirit of pride to whoever clings to her.

9.17.0.en: e. She calls those who walk in the truth to leave their way and walk after her. "To call passengers who go right on their ways: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: and as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him, Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant" [15-17].

9.17.1.en: f. She seduces, offering sweetness with theft, and pleasure with that which is hidden in evil. While the Wisdom of God builds a house to which He invites us to enjoy a banquet of mutual love, folly calls the young and seduces them to a banquet of stolen waters and secret bread held in the street, without a house.

9.18.0.en: g. She offers phantoms and death to whoever accepts her hospitality and eats of the secret bread she offers and the sweet stolen waters. "But he knoweth not that the shades are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell" [18].

9.19.0.en: A queen who cares for building. A foolish, simple woman.

9.19.1.en: She prepares a precious banquet. She calls to vain pleasures.

9.19.2.en: She offers the experience of the royal life. She offers slavery to pleasures.

9.20.0.en: * You have given me Your body and blood as a heavenly table; let me be satisfied, and rejoice, and grow in the knowledge of You.

9.20.1.en: I enjoy it and am united with You, O Savior of my soul.

9.20.2.en: * You have turned my soul into a temple for You, and set up Your altar within me, and proclaimed Your unique priesthood!

9.20.3.en: Accept my life as a sacrifice of love.

9.20.4.en: Pour upon it the wine of Your joy, and turn my depths into living sanctuaries.

9.20.5.en: * Carry me on Your shoulders, for I am foolish and weak!

9.20.6.en: Take me along Your royal way, that I may enjoy Your companionship.

9.20.7.en: * Support me, so that I am not drawn to the banquet of folly, nor listen to a strange voice.

9.20.8.en: Let me not seek passing pleasures, lest my soul descend to the pit.

9.20.9.en: * Break into my soul and enter into its depths.

9.20.10.en: Open to me the gates of heaven that I may enter them.

9.20.11.en: Dwell in my depths, and let me dwell in Your heavens!

9.20.12.en: You are my portion, my satisfaction, and the gladness of my heart.
